steps.title: Keep your current Ghostship installation
steps.instruction: If Ghostship already works in Portcove, keep using Play and the management operations available for that installation. Do not replace it or move its data to use this alternative Windows setup. For a separately prepared copy, follow the steps below.

steps.title: Download the official Windows package
steps.instruction: Use HarbourMasters/Ghostship on GitHub and its official 3.0.0 release. Download Nautilus-Alfa-Win64.zip and extract every file into a new folder outside your Portcove library. Keep existing installations and originals in place; do not extract over them.

steps.title: Prepare your own Super Mario 64 files
steps.instruction: Use your own Super Mario 64 US .z64 file and keep it unchanged. Open Ghostship.exe, choose the file and let setup finish. Keep sm64.o2r with the rest of the extracted files. Close Ghostship before adding it to Portcove.

steps.title: Add the prepared executable and play
steps.instruction: Open this game’s Files tab, expand Use an existing installation · Installation options, then choose Use an existing installation. Choose game executable and select Ghostship.exe from the prepared folder. Set Start in folder to that same folder and leave launch arguments empty. Review launch details and confirm the registration, then choose Play. Selecting a program records your intent to run it; it does not authenticate a publisher package.

warnings: Do not replace only the Ghostship 3.0.0 program with 2.0.0 while using newer saves. For a managed copy, use the legacy save recovery review in Saves & backups if Portcove offers it. For an installation you maintain, keep the newer files and use your own recovery copy.
This guide covers Windows. Existing data, source and execution safeguards still apply; a held update or recovery does not by itself prevent an otherwise safe Play.

steps.title: Download from the official Starship project

steps.title: Select the prepared game in Portcove
steps.instruction: Open this game’s Files tab, expand Use an existing installation · Installation options, then choose Use an existing installation. Choose game executable and select Starship.exe from the prepared folder. Set Start in folder to that folder and leave launch arguments empty. Review launch details and confirm the registration, then choose Play. Selecting this executable records your intent to run it; it does not authenticate it as an official publisher package.

warnings: Portcove cannot automatically install the v2.0.0 Windows package because the expected download check is missing. Choosing Starship.exe yourself does not confirm who published it.

ports.summary: Native recompilation of Blue Dragon.

steps.title: Keep a permitted complete installed Windows player
steps.instruction: Use an already permitted, fully working v1.3.1 Windows x86-64 reblue.exe installation with all of its creating runtime, original-derived game tree, profiles, mods and companions. Select the installed executable at its established root, not the freshly extracted setup copy or a repair/updater/build helper. The ordinary release uses DirectX12; a separately built Vulkan variant is not inherited. Project BSD3 terms do not license original game data, optional DLC or all private/generated/component material.

steps.title: Complete all three supported originals upstream
steps.instruction: Finish the normal upstream wizard with all three disc images from your own supported Global US/EU Blue Dragon copy before registration. Keep one supported set, its originals, recorded fingerprints and full resulting installation; Asia/JP or arbitrary cross-region/revision mixing is not established. Upstream marker/container/title checks and fingerprints are not Core exact three-disc authentication. The wizard copies itself, restarts, installs game files and writes its registration outside Core; wait for that preparation and any repair to finish. Core does not parse/assemble/generate/admit the triple.

steps.title: Settle replacement and recovery before selecting
steps.instruction: Finish any pending upstream update or recovery and a normal upstream start/quit before registration. Do not delete or ignore .update staging, ready markers, replaced-file or recovery history as a workaround: startup can apply a staged update and relaunch before the update-check setting is read. Turn the normal upstream startup update/content check off for this route. A new download, update, repair or backend/warm reboot must be completed externally before the next reviewed Play; Core does not adopt its successor.

steps.title: Select the installed player and its exact paths
steps.instruction: Select root/reblue.exe with the actual installed-root working directory and one literal --game_data_root=<absolute prepared game-data directory> argument (ordinarily root/game containing default.xex for this upstream installer), --profile=<actual existing profile name>, and --no-bd_update_check. Keep spaces inside each single token; these are arguments, not a shell command. The game-data directory must belong directly beneath that same creating installation root: its parent becomes the profile/cache root and must match the installed executable directory. Preserve an established supported custom direct-child tree rather than rename it or select an unrelated external directory. Explicit game_data_root selects that installation independently of shared install lookup; default.xex presence alone is not full original or private-output validation. The bound normal Windows entry runs its application/message loop in process. Keep any other supported working flags exactly; generic SDK user_data_root/cache_root flags do not override the title’s profile/cache routing.

steps.title: Preserve every actual original and player root
steps.instruction: Keep the whole external install, complete originals/private output, game-data tree, mods, installed DLC/content, logs, root/cache, profiles/<actual name>/reblue.toml, profile saves/achievements/content and unknown files, plus all legacy roots and existing shared HKCU installation registration. Preserve actual bd_saves_path and bd_cache_path overrides separately. The title uses the selected installation’s profiles/name as its user root; save/cache overrides and prior layouts are distinct. Do not reset profile/configuration, repoint shared registration or regenerate a private copy merely to register. Core neither backs up these roots nor claims safe save/profile migration or rollback.

steps.title: Review launch details and manage your copy
steps.instruction: Consent to the exact native executable, working directory and literal arguments, then choose Play separately. A current library-owned installation or active registration/launch cannot be bypassed by this alternative. Existing managed/source contracts remain unchanged; selecting an external copy grants no managed generation, immutable private-output certification or source admission. The program can make normal profile/DLC/cache writes, and its UI can reenable checks; this is not a sandbox or an all-network-off promise. Normal ordered shutdown has a default1.5second forced-exit watchdog, so process exit is not clean-save certification. Close all real instances before upstream changes, retain the old creating runtime/data together and relink changed executables. Registration-only removal preserves all external files.

warnings: This is the conditional Windows existing-player route. No game package/original/private save/compiler/installer/upstream helper/game was acquired or executed for this source/fixture batch; actual game/save/DLC/profile compatibility, installed Desktop, physical/human, other-platform and protected acceptance remain separate.

No Core-managed installation, three-disc preparation, generation, update, backup, rollback, migration, registry rewrite or external deletion is offered. The existing strict definition/source history and all earlier failures/qualification facts remain intact; no Supported or other-platform promotion.

source_requirements.label: Sonic the Hedgehog (Japan/USA/Europe) raw big-endian Genesis source

presentation.manual_preparation: Select your own Sonic the Hedgehog (Japan/USA/Europe) raw big-endian Genesis original. The managed route selects compatible official Windows packages and starts the base game directly. Historical installations without the partitioned-data contract retain their creating rules and remain held for a separate reviewed transition. The installation folder must use basic Latin characters and a short path; original files can stay where they are. Raw .bin or .md files and ZIPs containing the matching original are accepted; headered or byte-swapped images are not converted. Default settings, local state filenames and thumbnails stay in the declared managed scope. Gameplay, usable quickstates and in-game save/load remain unqualified; runtime replacement does not establish save compatibility or rewind progress. Default diagnostic recording is enabled. The managed logs directory contains input history, machine snapshots, original/build identities, settings and mod sidecars; these can contain private game memory and local paths. Nothing uploads automatically. Share these files only deliberately. Keep each replay and its sidecars together. Upstream retains the current capture and two previous captures, with 64 MiB input-history and 32 MiB state-attachment limits per capture and a 16 MiB background queue; recording stops on its bounds or storage failure. GENESIS_REPLAY_RECORD=0 is an optional user opt-out. Keep developer/debug, replay-playback and custom path overrides disabled. Backups include the checked private original copy and these diagnostics. Keep packaged libraries, assets and PolyForm Noncommercial/dependency notices together. No game original is included. Experimental fresh Widescreen/Fit is upstream default; saved choices stay in their creating installation.

The upstream extraction tools identify the US original by SHA-1 6d4f10a8b10e10dbe624cb23cf03b88bb8252973. Preserve the original outside the player folder; do not substitute a headered, translated, patched or other-region file.

steps.title: Finish upstream setup and select the real player
steps.instruction: Use only an already working upstream Windows zelda3.exe with its matching generated zelda3_assets.dat, SDL2.dll, zelda3.ini and companions. If setup is incomplete, follow the linked upstream source-build and asset-extraction instructions with your matching USA original before registration. The selected v0.3 release has a BPS asset, while its tagged source loader requires DAT; these instructions do not claim that placing a ROM beside that package completes setup. Do not mix generated assets between source revisions or select a launcher, extraction batch file or compiler as the player. Use the selected player’s containing folder as working directory and keep the already working literal arguments; do not invent shell commands.

steps.title: Register the existing player and use explicit Play
steps.instruction: You manage this external game and all its original files and saved data. Portcove saves the executable, working folder and launch arguments you select; it does not authenticate the complete package or original game files. Choose Play explicitly when you are ready. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion for this copy. Finish setup with the project’s tools and add only a working game. These instructions do not confirm successful setup, gameplay or save-state compatibility.

warnings: Add your prepared game to Portcove, then choose Play separately. These instructions do not establish Portcove-managed installation, the authenticity of original game files, gameplay or save-state compatibility.

ports.name: Zeus: Master of Olympus (eZeus)
ports.summary: Prepare Zeus: Master of Olympus through its upstream player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

presentation.manual_preparation: Prepare the full eZeus-0.8.2-beta.zip from its base release, then the later eZeus-0.8.2-beta.4.exe patch. The patch EXE alone is not a complete package. Follow the base release instructions: extract the eZeus folder under your working Zeus and Poseidon folder, perform upstream text conversion of Zeus_Text.eng and Zeus_MM.eng to the corresponding XML files, and place them where upstream specifies. Apply the patch player in the eZeus Bin folder, retaining all base resources. Register Bin/eZeus-0.8.2-beta.4.exe with Bin as working directory. engconverter-0.5.exe and VC_redist.x64.exe are preparation helpers, not players; run prerequisites deliberately only when needed. The player normally finds originals two directories above its EXE, or through zeus_path.txt. The eZeus root above Bin owns settings.txt, Save and companion resources such as Textures/Adventures. Preserve the entire working originals and eZeus tree, including any explicit original path, before replacing upstream files. No old-save conversion or base/expansion compatibility is inferred. Finish upstream preparation before registration. Register the real player with its matching working directory and separate literal argument lines. Play is a separate explicit action. You and upstream own this runtime, original files, saves and configuration. Registration-only removal preserves these external files; managed Update, Backup, Rollback, migration and deletion are unavailable for them. Preserve the working runtime and every actual data/profile location with the game closed before upstream replacement. Other platforms require their own upstream flow.

steps.title: Use the matching original game
steps.instruction: Both Zeus: Master of Olympus and the Poseidon expansion original files are required, including for the base-game identity. Upstream currently supports English and Polish. Preserve the original installation and work in a separate complete copy; eZeus differs from the original and does not promise exact parity.

steps.title: Prepare a separate upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the tagged source and its submodules, with the documented Qt and SDL2 dependencies. Place the built eZeus player under your complete working eZeus/Bin folder and launch from that folder. Use the matching base preparation and text conversion from upstream. Keep both original games and the actual settings, Save and resource directories backed up before changing the engine.

steps.title: Choose the matching upstream-linked Mac package
steps.instruction: Upstream links separate Intel and Apple Silicon 0.8.1-Beta.8 packages from MacThings, which documents macOS 14 or later. Use the matching 0.8.1 base preparation on a separate working copy. Copy the eZeus player and its bundled libs together into the prepared eZeus/Bin folder. Place Zeus_MM.xml and Zeus_Text.xml in the eZeus root above Bin, as described by upstream. Keep the complete original Zeus and Poseidon files, settings and Save directory together. This build has its own resources and profile. Keep the later Windows patch separate.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Select the game executable and its working folder, and put each launch argument on a separate line. Choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, originals, saves and settings. Removing its registration leaves those external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Close the game and keep a working copy and every data and profile folder before changing versions. Other platforms need their own setup instructions.
